messages:
PagerDuty Bot: [ALERT] control-plane error-rate elevated: 5xx spike detected across auth/org-lookup/billing gateways. 5xx rate ~12-18% over last 3m, latency spike to 1.2s. Impacting hosted inference requests and returning 502/504 to customers. Paging oncall. :fire:

sanjay: I’m on it — looking at traces. Initial signal shows org-lookup timeouts cascading into auth retries and then gateway 502s. Possible downstream DB connection saturation or slow cache.

tara: Confirmed in traces — org-lookup RPCs have high p95 ~900ms and many retries. We see retry fanout from the config service too. Can we toggle fallback to cached org data?

Ben Ops: I’m enabling the stale-cache fallback for org-lookup in prod Canary now (will report). Also pushing a quick rate limit to the gateway to stop internal retry storm. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Runbook check: Steps to contain control-plane cascade: 1) enable cached fallback, 2) throttle internal retries, 3) route traffic to dedicated controlplane pool, 4) notify CS.

Emily R: CS heads up: customer-impact visible for realtime features. Preparing messaging for customers if we can’t contain in 30m.

sanjay: Quick commands I'm running to validate health endpoints and throttle config: 
```bash
# health check controlplane endpoints
curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/health | jq .
# set gateway throttles (temporary window)
./infractl set-rate --service gateway --limit 300rps --reason "mitigation org-lookup timeouts"
```

Ben Ops: Stale cache fallback toggle applied to 2/3 regions. Observability: errors dropped to ~6% in those regions. Rolling to remaining region.

tara: Also disabling noncritical config fanout (feature flag propagation) — that was causing extra org-lookup calls. Patch applied, reducing RPCs by ~35%.

sanjay: Agree we should also reduce concurrency for org-lookup pool to avoid DB queueing: dropping max concurrency to 40% of baseline. Applying now.

PagerDuty Bot: Note added: mitigation steps applied by Ben Ops, tara, sanjay.

Ben Ops: Concurrency cut, retries limited, fallback enabled. 5xx in controlplane now down to ~3-4% and trending. Latency p95 reduced to ~220ms in canaries.

Emily R: CS draft ready, waiting on stability signal to send targeted note to top-tier customers.

sanjay: Root cause hypothesis: a slow metadata DB shard + a recent config rollout causing increased fanout for lookups (feature flag change). The combined effect caused rpc queues and retries. We should rollback the config rollout and investigate DB shard metrics.

Ben Ops: Rolling back the latest config rollout for feature-flag propagation (started 18m ago).

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: after initial mitigation, if stable for 45m, move to monitoring status and assign postmortem to eng-runtime with priority P2.

tara: Found a spike in DB write latency correlating with the config rollout timestamp. Capturing logs and traces to attach to postmortem.

sanjay: Assigning follow-ups: (1) DB team to investigate shard hotness (Ben Ops), (2) Runtime to add backpressure and circuit-breaker for org-lookup (sanjay), (3) Product to re-evaluate feature-flag rollout gating (tara).

Ben Ops: I’ll kick off a mitigation ticket for DB shard and request a temporary shard split if needed.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident status: contained -> partial mitigation in all regions, customer impact reduced but still possible for small percentage of requests. Paging cleared to oncall but keep watch for 1H.

Emily R: Sending targeted CS note now to customers impacted in the last 30m and offering engineers for high-severity customers.

sanjay: Leaving detailed logs and runbook steps in the incident ticket. Handoff to next oncall in 30m — @tara you want this?

tara: I can take the handoff. I'll monitor the dashboards and start the postmortem doc once we confirm stability.

Ben Ops: Will follow-up on DB mitigation and config rollout rollback.

cs-notify-bot: Customer messages sent to affected orgs: 5 customers flagged for potential functional impact; CS notified.

sanjay: Notes for postmortem: timeline, config rollout correlation, DB shard hotspot, lack of circuit-breaker for org-lookup, retry amplification. Action items and owners as above.

oncall-bot: Handoff complete. Next-check window ends at +60m. If error-rate <1% for 45m, mark incident resolved and schedule postmortem. :white_check_mark:
